runs.text: Problem B1
Suppose that each point in the plane is colored either red or green, subject to the following condition: for every three noncollinear points
of the same color, the center of the circle passing through
is also this color. Prove that all points of the plane are the same color.

hints.title: Bound the opposite color on a circle

runs.text: If a circle is centered at a red point, how many green points can lie on it? Three distinct collinear points cannot lie on a circle, so the hypothesis applies to any three points on that circle.
Choose a red point R and a green point G at distance d. Use several circles centered at R and G, with radii strictly between d/2 and d.
Every circle from the R-family meets every circle from the G-family twice. Choose the radii generically so the 18 intersection points are distinct, then count how many can be each color.

items.text: A circle centered at R contains at most two green points, so three R-circles contain at most six green intersections.
A circle centered at G contains at most two red points, so three G-circles contain at most six red intersections.
The 18 distinct intersections must all be red or green, but 6+6<18.

runs.text: A line meets a circle in at most two points. Therefore three distinct points on one circle are automatically noncollinear.
Two circles with center distance d and radii r,s meet in two points when |r-s|<d<r+s.
